name: SkeletonDB
tagline: Experimental lock-free in-memory MVCC key-value store for Go built on a Bw-tree; untouched since 2016.
description: SkeletonDB is a small Go library by Tristan Rice that implements an in-memory multi-version key-value store on top of a Bw-tree, the latch-free index structure from Microsoft Research that updates pages with atomic compare-and-swap instead of locks. It was a 2016 hobby project and never grew persistence, a server, or a stable API. Its value today is as a compact, readable Go implementation of Bw-tree ideas; for real embedded storage in Go, pick a maintained engine.
statusNote: Hobby project with no commits since December 2016; effectively unmaintained. Use Badger, Pebble, bbolt or BuntDB for embedded storage in Go.
strengths: Readable Go implementation of a latch-free Bw-tree
MVCC snapshots without locks for concurrent readers and writers
MIT license and tiny codebase, easy to study or fork
weaknesses: In-memory only: no persistence or recovery
No production users or test history to rely on
useCases: Learning how Bw-trees and MVCC work
Prototyping lock-free data structures in Go
notIdealFor: Data that must survive a restart
